prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but first a few quick points so you hire the right lawyer for your specific case.

Short answer
- Look for a California personal injury lawyer who focuses on car accidents (often called a car-accident or auto-accident attorney) with recent experience handling cases in Alameda County (Pleasanton) and with trial experience if the insurer won’t settle.
- Hire on a contingency-fee basis (no fee unless you recover) and get a free consultation to compare a few firms.

What matters when choosing a lawyer
- Relevant experience: years doing car-accident cases, number and type of similar verdicts/settlements (whiplash vs. catastrophic injuries vs. wrongful death).
- Trial experience: many insurers settle, but you want a lawyer who will go to court if needed.
- Communication and team: who will handle day-to-day (attorney vs. paralegal), how often they will update you.
- Fees and costs: typical contingency is about 33% for pre-suit settlements and up to ~40% if a suit and trial are required; ask who advances case costs and how liens (medical providers, hospitals, ER) are handled.
- Local knowledge: familiarity with local courts, judges, expert witnesses, and opposing defense firms/insurers.
- Reputation and reviews: client reviews, peer ratings (e.g., Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers), and willingness to provide references.

Questions to ask in a free consultation
- Have you handled cases like mine in Alameda/Contra Costa County? What were the results?
- Who will handle the case day-to-day?
- What is your fee and what costs will I owe if we don’t recover?
- Do you have trial experience? How often do you take cases to trial?
- What’s your estimate of value and timeline for my case?
- How do you handle medical liens and treatment recommendations?
- Can I see client references or online reviews?

Immediate steps you should take (if you haven’t already)
- Seek and document medical treatment now (important for both health and claims).
- Preserve evidence: photos of scene, vehicle damage, injuries, traffic signs, skid marks. Save medical bills, pay stubs for lost wages.
- Get a copy of the police report and contact info for witnesses.
- Do not accept or sign any settlement offer without consulting a lawyer. Don’t give recorded statements to the other driver’s insurer.
- Avoid posting details/photos on social media.

Deadlines to know (California)
- Personal injury: generally 2 years from the date of the accident to file a lawsuit (Cal. Code Civ. Proc. §335.1).
- Property damage: generally 3 years.
- Claims against a government entity: much shorter—often 6 months to file an administrative claim. Ask a lawyer immediately if a government vehicle or public road is involved.

If you’d like, I can:
- Find and list 3–5 local Pleasanton/Alameda County personal injury attorneys with brief notes (experience, fees, reviews) so you can call for consultations.
- Or help you draft a short script of questions to ask when you call.

Tell me which you prefer and give any relevant details: date of accident, severity of injuries (minor, hospitalized, permanent disability), whether fault is disputed, whether the at-fault party was insured.
